newsitem.title: KENYA: Madagascar cyclone left 200 dead or missing.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar cyclone left 200 dead or missing.

text.p: The worst cyclone to hit Madagascar in living memory left 200 people dead or missing and affected some 520,000 people, the Red Cross said on Friday.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said Cyclone Gretelle destroyed up to 90 percent of villages in the southeast when it hit on January 24.
"The magnitude of the disaster is only now becoming apparent due to the destruction of all communications to the area and poor land transport," the IFRC said in a statement in Nairobi.
It said floodwaters reached 16 metres (52 feet) in places and 520,000 people were affected including many made homeless.

"The destruction of all crops and available food stocks, coupled with the endemic malnutrition in the south of Madagascar and the custom of drinking surface water makes the surviving population extremely vulnerable," IFRC said.
It said medium to long-term aid would be needed until houses could be rebuilt and crops re-established and appealed for a total of $620,000 for the federation and Malagasy Red Cross.
State radio said on Wednesday more than 140 bodies had been found but warned the final death toll would be even higher.
